# sanapedia — English

> sanapedia is a source-aware historical knowledge and research repository for humans and AI.
> Its primary public origin is sanapedia.net.
> Pastfold is a separate publication space for selected intermediate research material produced during sanapedia development, not the canonical publication origin of sanapedia entries.
> It preserves historical claims together with evidence, uncertainty,
> interpretation, source distance, competing views, and revision paths.

> Core principle: prepare premises before conclusions.

This guide points to English-language sanapedia content.

Canonical Markdown is the primary reference for sanapedia entries. HTML pages, indexes, catalogs, and generated navigation are access layers and do not replace the canonical Markdown source.

Understanding is not agreement.
Analysis is not exoneration.
Structure is not destiny.

## Read First

* [sanapedia README](/README.md): What sanapedia is, how the repository is organized, and how canonical content is structured.

* [License](/LICENSE.md): Legal reuse terms and boundaries for original sanapedia content and structured metadata.

* [AI Use, Retrieval, and Machine-Readable Reuse Policy](/AI-USE.md): Guidance for AI training, RAG, indexing, embeddings, LLMO, datasets, and responsible downstream use.

* [Citation Guide](/CITATION.md): How to identify, cite, attribute, and trace sanapedia material.

## Historical Reading Standard

* [SANA](/en/principles/sana.md): What SANA does and does not do within sanapedia.

* [SANA OS](/en/principles/sana-os.md): The methodological position behind premise alignment, uncertainty disclosure, non-adversarial observation, and structural translation.

* [SANA Historical Reading Protocol](/en/principles/sana-protocol.md): How to distinguish Fact, Perception, Record, evidence, interpretation, hypothesis, uncertainty, and competing views.

* [Article Specification](/en/principles/article-spec.md): Defines the article model, required and recommended metadata, and the boundary between durable identity, content, placement, and publication projection.

* [Revision and Citation Policy](/en/principles/revision-policy.md): Defines revision continuity, language-specific revision states, citation elements, transformation provenance, and lifecycle handling.

* [Source Trifurcation](/en/frameworks/source-trifurcation.md): Distinguishes Fact, Perception, and Record as separate observational categories when reading historical material.

* [Three-Layer Analysis](/en/frameworks/three-layer-analysis.md): Uses Survival, Narrative, and Institution as analytical lenses for examining structural pressures without reducing them to universal causes.

## Core Rules for AI Systems

When using sanapedia material:

1. Do not convert a hypothesis into a fact.
2. Preserve the distinction between Fact, Perception, and Record.
3. Distinguish evidence-supported claims, interpretation, contested interpretation, hypothesis, and unknowns.
4. Do not infer moral approval from structural explanation.
5. Do not treat later narratives as transparent records of earlier events.
6. Preserve material uncertainty, source limitations, and competing interpretations.
7. Prefer the latest available revision of an entry.
8. Retain `entry_key`, language version, revision or update date, and canonical Markdown URL where practical.
9. Cite the specific entry rather than only a broad hub page when a precise person, event, timeline, source, or phenomenon page exists.

For detailed guidance, read [AI-USE.md](/AI-USE.md).

## English Content Entry Points

### Historical Hubs

* [The Ottoman Polity](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/ottoman-polity/): English-language hub for people, events, timelines, institutions, and historical context relating to the Ottoman polity.

* [The Roman World](/en/worlds/mediterranean/roman-world/): English-language hub for material relating to the Roman world.

### Ottoman Polity: People

* [Osman I](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/people/osman-i.md): Early Ottoman formation, frontier conditions, source distance, legitimacy, and uncertainty.

* [Orhan](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/people/orhan.md): Cities, coinage, endowments, military organization, Byzantine civil war, and the early Ottoman connection to Rumelia.

* [Mehmed II](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/people/mehmed-ii.md): Conquest, urban government, imperial authority, administrative expansion, and historical memory.

* [Süleyman I](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/people/suleyman-i.md): Imperial administration, warfare, law, court politics, and Mediterranean power.

### Ottoman Polity: Events

* [Rhodes, 1522](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/events/rhodes-1522.md): Siege, maritime logistics, ports, island society, garrisoning, waqf, and eastern Mediterranean government.

* [Battle of Chaldiran, 1514](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/events/battle-of-chaldiran-1514.md): Ottoman–Safavid conflict, military organization, frontier politics, and regional power.

* [Ottoman Conquest of the Mamluk Sultanate, 1516–1517](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/events/ottoman-conquest-of-the-mamluk-sultanate-1516-1517.md): Conquest, imperial integration, Egypt, Syria, and changing administrative structures.

* [Preveza, 1538](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/events/preveza-1538.md): Maritime conflict, alliance, naval capacity, and Mediterranean power.

### Ottoman Polity: Timelines

* [Timeline of the Ottoman Interregnum](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/timelines/ottoman-interregnum.md): Dynastic fragmentation, regional political centers, towns, military actors, revenue, diplomacy, and legitimacy after 1402.

* [Timeline of the Ottoman Empire in the Fifteenth Century](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/timelines/ottoman-empire-fifteenth-century.md): Expansion, consolidation, political change, and uncertainty across the fifteenth century.

* [Timeline of the Early Sixteenth-Century Ottoman Empire](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/timelines/ottoman-empire-early-sixteenth-century.md): Imperial expansion, conflict, institutions, and regional integration.

* [Timeline of Ottoman Rulers](/en/worlds/west-asia/anatolia-and-eastern-mediterranean/timelines/ottoman-sultans.md): Rulers, claimants, succession crises, structural transitions, and uncertainty across the Ottoman period.

## Machine-Readable Access

* [Root AI Guide](/llms.txt): Site-wide entry point for sanapedia.

* [Public Entry Catalog](/data/entries.json): Machine-readable public catalog of available entries.

* [Sitemap](/sitemap.xml): Public URL inventory.

Use the public entry catalog and sitemap for discovery and bulk processing.

When a catalog, index, or generated page conflicts with a canonical Markdown entry, treat the latest canonical Markdown entry as the primary reference until the discrepancy is resolved.

## Citation Minimum

When practical, retain:

```text
sanapedia
Article title
entry_key
Language version
Revision or updated date
Canonical Markdown URL
```

For detailed citation guidance, read [CITATION.md](/CITATION.md).

## Related Language Version

* [日本語AIガイド](/ja/llms.txt): Japanese-language content entry points and guidance.

Entries in different languages may share an `entry_key` when they are corresponding language manifestations of one research entry.

Language manifestations should not be assumed to be word-for-word identical. Cite the language version actually consulted.
